The European part is drained into the [Arctic Ocean](/wiki/Arctic_Ocean "Arctic Ocean"), [Baltic Sea](/wiki/Baltic_Sea "Baltic Sea"), [Black Sea](/wiki/Black_Sea "Black Sea"), and [Caspian Sea](/wiki/Caspian_Sea "Caspian Sea"). The Asian part is drained into the [Arctic Ocean](/wiki/Arctic_Ocean "Arctic Ocean") and the [Pacific Ocean](/wiki/Pacific_Ocean "Pacific Ocean").

Notable rivers of Russia in Europe are the [Volga](/wiki/Volga "Volga") (which is the longest river in Europe), [Pechora](/wiki/Pechora_(river) "Pechora (river)"), [Don](/wiki/Don_River,_Russia "Don River, Russia"), [Kama](/wiki/Kama_River "Kama River"), [Oka](/wiki/Oka_River "Oka River") and the [Northern Dvina](/wiki/Northern_Dvina "Northern Dvina"), while several other rivers originate in Russia but flow into other countries, such as the [Dnieper](/wiki/Dnieper "Dnieper") (flowing through Russia, then [Belarus](/wiki/Belarus "Belarus") and [Ukraine](/wiki/Ukraine "Ukraine") and into the [Black Sea](/wiki/Black_Sea "Black Sea")) and the [Western Dvina](/wiki/Western_Dvina "Western Dvina") (flowing through Russia, then [Belarus](/wiki/Belarus "Belarus") and [Latvia](/wiki/Latvia "Latvia") into the [Baltic Sea](/wiki/Baltic_Sea "Baltic Sea")).

The Inca estate of [Machu Picchu](/wiki/Machu_Picchu "Machu Picchu"), [Peru](/wiki/Peru "Peru"), is one of the [New Seven Wonders of the World](/wiki/New_Seven_Wonders_of_the_World#Winners "New Seven Wonders of the World").

The rise of plant growing and the subsequent appearance of permanent human settlements allowed for the multiple and overlapping beginnings of civilizations in South America.

One of the earliest known South American civilizations was [Caral–Supe](/wiki/Caral%E2%80%93Supe "Caral–Supe"), on the central Peruvian coast. Though a pre-ceramic culture, the monumental architecture of Caral–Supe created one of the first cities of the world, generally dated to around 3500 BC, at [Huaricanga](/wiki/Huaricanga "Huaricanga") in the [Fortaleza](/wiki/Fortaleza_River_(Peru) "Fortaleza River (Peru)") area, contemporaneous with the pyramids of [Ancient Egypt](/wiki/Ancient_Egypt "Ancient Egypt"), one of the [oldest-known civilizations](/wiki/Cradle_of_civilization "Cradle of civilization") in the Americas and one of the six sites where civilization separately originated in the ancient world.[[20]](#cite_note-AncientAndes-31) Caral–Supe governing class established a trade network and developed agriculture then followed by [Chavín](/wiki/Chav%C3%ADn "Chavín") by 900 BC, according to some estimates and archaeological finds. Artifacts were found at a site called [Chavín de Huantar](/wiki/Chav%C3%ADn_de_Huantar "Chavín de Huantar") in modern Peru at an elevation of 3,177 meters (10,423 ft).
